title: Descent along a faithfully flat ring map of finite type, finite presentation, formal unramifiedness, unramifiedness and etaleness
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The theorem states that if the S-algebra A tensor over R with S is of finite type, of finite presentation, formally unramified, unramified or etale, then the corresponding property holds for A as an R-algebra, with the converse being the easy direction (statement lines 1662-1678). The proof is not one argument but a sequence of independent ones. Part (a) chooses a finite system of generators of the base changed algebra, writes each as a finite sum of decomposable tensors, builds the polynomial R-algebra on the resulting variables together with the evident map to A, and concludes that the cokernel vanishes because it vanishes after tensoring with the faithfully flat S (proof lines 1681-1687). Part (b) is the substantive one: finite type over R is taken from part (a), a surjection from a polynomial algebra onto A is chosen, finite generation of the kernel after base change is obtained from an Algebra lemma, generators are lifted from the base changed kernel back to the kernel itself, and the quotient by the ideal they generate is a finitely presented R-algebra which becomes isomorphic to A after base change and therefore already is A (proof lines 1690-1703). Part (c) identifies the module of relative differentials of the base changed algebra with the base change of the module of relative differentials of A, and descends the vanishing (proof lines 1706-1711). Parts (d) and (e) are deductions from (a) and (c) together with the standard criteria for unramifiedness and etaleness (proof lines 1714-1717 and 1720-1724). The claim is H3: at least three of the five items are independent arguments rather than steps of one, and part (b) additionally requires the lifting construction for finite presentation together with the external algebra criterion that finite generation of a kernel can be checked after faithfully flat base change, which is precisely the extra criterion that separates this from a routine derivation.
